chapter: After Cab: Don Redman, teaching and records
title: The lost Stormy Weather record with Benny Carter and Jacquet
summary: He recalls a California recording with Benny Carter, Illinois Jacquet and Hilton Jefferson that none of them has, and noisy old records.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: And that's how I found out how them great... I learned something about writing for bass from that guy, that arranger out there -- I can't think of his name now. That's the time when Benny Carter came out, and we made a recording of...
Illinois Jacquet and Benny Carter, Jeff...
God, I wish I had that. Somebody should have that.
I do, too, boy, because that was such a beautiful thing.
It's a shame that record is lost, or none of us have it, because it's a fabulous record. We went in the studio then. Jacquet, Hilton Jefferson and Benny Carter. Boy, they sure played on that thing.

I've got a record now with Jefferson, but there's so much noise on it. And we cracked it again, and got a good tape, but I never kept a record of myself with a good tape. Because the old records had so darn much noise on them. Sometimes you had to make the companies press it again to get the noise out. But they didn't have the tapes... All them old things had noise on them.
